title: Module quiz: Scenario: Claude Code in CI

questions.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. A job must decide whether to fail, but the seriousness of each comment is free text. What fixes that?

options.text: Ask the model to put the word critical at the very start of any serious comment it makes
options.says: Ruled out because a word in prose is a convention: "A sentence that asks for more care is a request; the criteria are the case list."

options.text: Ask for JSON that follows a schema where severity is one of a few fixed values
options.says: A closed list can be compared with a floor.

options.text: Count the comments and fail the job once they pass a fixed number chosen by the team
options.says: Ruled out because a count says nothing about how bad a finding is: "what each severity means, with one example for each".

options.text: Search the prose of every comment for the words that usually go with a bad finding
options.says: Ruled out because the severity belongs in the schema: "The severity then belongs in the schema as a closed list, so a script can compare it with a floor."

questions.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The job script ignores how the command ended, and the job is green although the run stopped at its turn limit. What is the remedy?

options.text: Read the exit status and the JSON, and fail whenever no valid answer exists
options.says: The gate fails the job whenever no valid answer exists.

options.text: Raise the turn limit until the run always finishes well before it reaches that limit
options.says: Ruled out because the limit exists to stop a loop: "`--max-turns` stops a loop".

options.text: Run the command again whenever the output that comes back looks a little too short
options.says: Ruled out because a rerun changes nothing: "re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result".

options.text: Remove the turn limit so that a run stops only when all of its work is finished
options.says: Ruled out because the limit is what ends the run by itself: "A run with no person must end by itself".

questions.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The audit of the draft prints `batchable: debt-report`. What does that finding report?

options.text: A scheduled job runs in real time and pays full price
options.says: The finding is about a scheduled job: "`batchable`: a scheduled job that runs in real time and pays full price."

options.text: A job that someone waits for runs as a batch
options.says: Ruled out because that is the other finding: "`blocking-batch`: a job someone waits for that runs as a batch."

options.text: A command that starts claude lacks the print flag
options.says: Ruled out because that is a third: "`no-print-flag`: a command that starts `claude` without `-p` or `--print`."

options.text: A review is made in one pass and in a shared session
options.says: Ruled out because the design of a review has its own findings: "`single-pass-review`, `shared-session`, `no-prior-findings` and `writes`: the design of a review".

origin.section: The audit: a checklist that reads the pipeline

questions.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The draft's review lists the tools Read, Grep and Bash. What does the audit report about it?

options.text: A job that a person waits for runs as a batch with no promise of speed
options.says: Ruled out because that finding is about the API: "`blocking-batch`: a job someone waits for that runs as a batch."

options.text: A command that starts claude lacks the print flag that makes a run headless
options.says: Ruled out because that finding is about the command line: "`no-print-flag`: a command that starts `claude` without `-p` or `--print`."

options.text: The job holds a means of changing things although it only looks at code
options.says: A review needs reading tools only: "A shell tool is a way to change things".

options.text: A session that wrote the code is also the one that judges that code afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because the session is another property: "the review runs as its own session and not as a continuation of the one that generated the change".

origin.section: The review reads, and nothing else
